claim.quote: We find a well-detected peak in the correlation function at 100h^{-1} Mpc separation that is an excellent match to the predicted shape and location of the imprint of the recombination-epoch acoustic oscillations on the low-redshift clustering of matter.

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date; journal publication dates were not read from a fetched source.

key_value_text.quote: The acoustic peak provides a standard ruler by which we can measure the ratio of the distances to z=0.35 and z=1089 to 4% fractional accuracy and the absolute distance to z=0.35 to 5% accuracy.
key_value_text.value: Acoustic peak at 100 h⁻¹ Mpc separation in the luminous-red-galaxy correlation function; ratio of distances to z=0.35 and z=1089 to 4% accuracy

name: Detection of the baryon acoustic peak in SDSS luminous red galaxies
notes: Result type is measurement: the title says "Detection", but the abstract does not say "first", so first_detection is not used. The paper used SDSS-I spectroscopy of luminous red galaxies.

summary.plain: SDSS astronomers found a faint, preferred separation of about 100 h⁻¹ Mpc in the clustering of 46,748 luminous red galaxies, the imprint of sound waves in the early universe, and used it as a ruler to measure cosmic distances to about 5% accuracy.
summary.technical: Large-scale correlation function of 46,748 SDSS luminous red galaxies (3816 deg², 0.16<z<0.47): a well-detected acoustic peak at 100 h⁻¹ Mpc; distance ratio to z=0.35 and z=1089 to 4% and absolute distance to z=0.35 to 5%; Ωm h² to 8%.

title: Detection of the Baryon Acoustic Peak in the Large-Scale Correlation Function of SDSS Luminous Red Galaxies
why_it_matters: The abstract says the detection demonstrates linear growth of structure by gravitational instability between z=1000 and the present, and that the acoustic peak provides a standard ruler for cosmological distance.
